clue.text: I'm a bank that returns folded sheets, Japanese

indicators.note: the self-describing clue says the whole phrase turns round, so the pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: the words give their own letters, apostrophe dropped
Giro was the British Post Office bank (Girobank)

explanation.surface: A bank boasts of handing back documents in a folded state, with a Japanese flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that returns' turns IMAGIRO round as one run. GIRO was a UK bank and payment system.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art of paper folding produces folded sheets in the shape of birds and animals.

clue.text: Harps on about children whose parents are dead

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone keeps talking about harps.
explanation.definitionFit: A child left without living mother and father is the standard dictionary meaning.

clue.text: Outside of the law, wicked bird so it's said

indicators.note: so it's said tells us the phrase is spoken and heard, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: ill means wicked and the bird is an eagle, so the phrase is ill eagle

explanation.surface: A villainous bird is said to operate beyond legal bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful falls outside what statute permits.

clue.text: Exorbitant charge on a mooring like this

definitions.text: Exorbitant charge on a mooring like this

indicators.note: exorbitant means wildly excessive, beyond bounds, hinting the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A complaint about being overcharged for a berth in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exorbitant' rearranges CHARGEONA; the whole clue also describes the fee for a berth, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where ships drop anchor is a mooring, and an anchorage fee is charged for it.

clue.text: Decidedly states isn't mad about sis

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the other word
mad means crazy and disordered, so the letters of isn't are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone firmly declares that they are not angry with their sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' gives INTS, which 'about' wraps round the sister.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something firmly and repeatedly is to state it decidedly.

clue.text: Start to sugar small number-of coffees or teas?

definitions.text: Start to sugar small number-of coffees or teas?

indicators.note: the start of the word sugar means its first letter alone

parts.note: wee is Scots for small
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Adding sugar to a small number of coffees or teas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes what sugar does to a drink while also giving the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a drink sugary is to add sweetness to it.

clue.text: So get a bit flushed being drunken no more

parts.note: taken as written
to be red is to get flushed in the face

explanation.surface: Someone blushes as they stop being drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: BE RED is read as one phrase meaning to turn flushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Once intoxication wears off a person is made sober again.

clue.text: And fit to crack jokes at the back of the store

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to quip is to crack a joke

explanation.surface: A joker's corner at the back of the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places the joke-word after the E from the end of 'store'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit out with gear is to supply or furnish someone.

clue.text: Let off about play I found touching way?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters are wrapped round the rest
off means gone wrong or not right, so the letters of let are rearranged

parts.note: an act is part of a play
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone excused a show and found it moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' gives TLE, and 'about' places the play-piece and I within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of touch, the touching way of perceiving.

clue.text: Small numbers say yes to this type of bouquet

parts.note: nos is the short form of numbers
eg (for example) is a stock substitute for say
ay or aye means yes

explanation.surface: A request for a modest number of flower arrangements is approved.
explanation.definitionFit: A small posy of flowers is another name for a small bunch or bouquet.

clue.text: Where archbishops' leader in places are found?

definitions.text: Where archbishops' leader in places are found?

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the other word
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A question about where senior clergy reside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: archbishops live in palaces, such as Lambeth Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Archbishops traditionally live in grand official residences such as Lambeth.

clue.text: Kicks out of disco once bus comes around

indicators.note: comes around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A doorman ejects people from a nightclub as the last bus arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman who ejects troublemakers from a club throws them out.

clue.text: What's starting a gory great rumpus, OK…

definitions.text: What's starting a gory great rumpus, OK…

indicators.note: the starting letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Asking what begins a bloody brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a rumpus, so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble or a fight.

clue.text: … putting an end to a rough kind of fray?

definitions.meaning: brawling or fighting, a scrap being a scuffle

explanation.surface: Ending a tough sort of brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapping is both discarding something and fighting, a scrap being a fight.

clue.text: Rulers whose wives may seem fruity I'd say?

definitions.text: Rulers whose wives may seem fruity I'd say?

parts.words: Rulers whose wives may seem fruity I'd say?
parts.note: the wife of an Eastern monarch has a title that is also the name of a dried grape

explanation.surface: A joke about monarchs with flirtatious spouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottoman monarchs were rulers, and their wives were called by a name shared with a dried fruit.

clue.text: Yearned badly for house where clergy can stay

indicators.note: badly means done wrong, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone longed desperately for a home among clergymen.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean's official residence is a house for clergy.

clue.text: Describing him thus, led gaunt one awry?

parts.note: one gives A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: awry means twisted or askew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thin man being led off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is the gaunt one: a bony figure looks all corners.
explanation.definitionFit: Angular describes a lean, bony person whose frame is full of sharp corners.

clue.text: One who painted what we'd call his old Dutch?

definitions.text: One who painted what we'd call his old Dutch?

parts.words: One who painted what we'd call his old Dutch?
parts.note: a Dutch Old Master, with a play on old Dutch, the Cockney term for a wife

explanation.surface: A painter of a man's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is Cockney for wife; here it suggests a Dutch Old Master.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was a 17th-century Dutch painter.

clue.text: Girl to sit topless for one who drops by

parts.note: Vi is a short girl's name
taken as written

indicators.note: topless means losing its top, so the first letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A model is asked to pose without a top for a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller or guest pays a visit when dropping in.

clue.text: Concerning a roster, a practical man

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a roster is a list

explanation.surface: A sensible person deals with a duty rota.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatist who accepts things as they are is practical.

clue.text: Of part of the eye, it's true bathing can

indicators.note: bathing means surrounding with water, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: real means true
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An eye fact about a can being washed.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

clue.text: At corners round river they catch so much!

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one word goes around the letter

parts.note: angles are corners

explanation.surface: Fishermen boasting from the corners of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation teases fishermen's tall tales about their catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishermen with rod and line are famed for exaggerating their catch.

clue.text: For trouble, a regular volunteers, note…

parts.note: a GI is a regular American soldier
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A soldier and volunteers cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is Britain's Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb or stir up is to upset, a sense of trouble as a verb.

clue.text: … sooner than peer that's initially remote

parts.note: an earl is a peer of the realm
ie stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A distant aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'than' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done before the expected time happened sooner.

clue.text: Damaged as lubricant ran all around

indicators.note: all around means encircling, so the word sits inside the other

parts.note: sped means ran or hurried
oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: Oil spilled everywhere, causing ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruined goods have been harmed, spoilt.

clue.text: Mostly pasta I get cooked with last bit of dough

definitions.text: Mostly pasta I get cooked with last bit of dough

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means nearly all, so the final letter of the word is dropped
the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone cooks pasta using the last of the dough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts PASTA to PAST; 'cooked' rearranges PASTIGET plus H.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strings of pasta are the clue's whole subject.

clue.text: You'll see her returning from trek I have found!

definitions.text: You'll see her returning from trek I have found!

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the run of letters reads backwards
from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone back from a long walk reports a sighting.
explanation.walkthrough: A walker is someone you would see coming back from a trek.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler on foot is the person back from a trek.

clue.text: Speed of a regular gopak? Not so!

indicators.note: of means the letters are part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking the tempo of a lively Ukrainian dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A gopak is a fast Ukrainian dance; 'Not so!' jokes that this very slow tempo is no dance speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical marking for a very slow tempo.

clue.text: Set well, famous batsman gets 10 going round

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the number encloses the name

parts.note: 10 is ten in words
Graeme Hick was a famous England batsman

explanation.surface: A great cricketer scores ten runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Graeme HICK was an England Test batsman (cricket).
explanation.definitionFit: When a liquid congeals, it becomes firm or sets.

clue.text: One has most of the sick where workers are found

parts.note: one gives AN, the indefinite article

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A person with most of the illness in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' are worker ants, not factory hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants live in the mound built by their colony.

clue.text: Later returns about taxmen's withdrawal

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed letters surround the others
returns means comes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax office

explanation.surface: Tax officials hand money back later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' gives RETAL, which 'about' places round the tax office. Retiral is a Scottish word for retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiral is a chiefly Scottish word for retirement or a stepping back.

clue.text: Under bad editor had a long haul

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A poor editor suffered through a tough job.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lasted through a long ordeal is to have borne it.
